[LLM] YesWiki Bazar form-import volumetric POST — CVE-2026-46670 blind SQLi extraction loop Exploitation High
Hunts the byte-by-byte extraction loop used to exploit CVE-2026-46670 in YesWiki. The PoC drives one POST to /?BazaR&vue=formulaire per character of the hex-encoded value being exfiltrated from yeswiki_users, producing dozens-to-hundreds of POSTs to a single URI from a single source IP in a short window — an unusual pattern for a wiki application. Rationale: Locks on the article's exact request shape (POST + csUriQuery containing both 'BazaR' and 'vue=formulaire') and the unavoidable property of the PoC: blind extraction requires N requests for N characters of the password hash, so a per-source-IP POST count >=20 in 5 min to this single endpoint is a strong signal that something other than a human is wiki-ing. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jwvv-qr7q-cv8j • https://github.com/YesWiki/yeswiki/blob/1f485c049db030b94c047ec219e63534ac81142e/tools/bazar/services/FormManager.php#L258

[LLM] Non-browser User-Agent against YesWiki Bazar form-import endpoint — CVE-2026-46670 exploit tooling Exploitation High
Hunts the PoC's exploit fingerprint: a request to /?BazaR&vue=formulaire from a scripting-language User-Agent (the published PoC uses Python-urllib/3.13). Real users post Bazar forms from a browser; a curl/python/PowerShell UA on this exact endpoint is high-signal for CVE-2026-46670 exploitation or reconnaissance. Rationale: The published PoC literally ships with User-Agent: Python-urllib/3.13 (from the Burp capture in the article body). The Bazar form-import endpoint is a low-traffic admin path on YesWiki; a scripting-language UA hitting it via POST is rarely benign and matches both the public PoC and copycat exploitation. Cross-checked against the GHSA advisory at github.com/advisories/GHSA-jwvv-qr7q-cv8j. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jwvv-qr7q-cv8j

[LLM] MiniUpdate UpdateChecker.dll sideload via legitimate signed .NET host Installation High
Detects loading of the Screening Serpens MiniUpdate payload (internal name UpdateChecker.dll) by a legitimate signed .NET host process via DLL sideloading. The DLL is dropped alongside a hijack-vulnerable benign binary from the Hiring Portal.zip lure and loaded from non-standard user-writable directories. Rationale: Pivots on Unit 42's named internal DLL `UpdateChecker.dll` plus the eight published SHA256 hashes for the MiniUpdate RAT family. User-writable path filter mirrors Screening Serpens' Hiring Portal.zip ZIP-extract sideload chain. Cross-checked against Check Point's 2025 UNC1549 report and MITRE T1574.014 (AppDomainManager Injection). Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1019/ • https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/iranian-cyber-actors-target-europe/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/014/

[LLM] Screening Serpens AppDomainManager hijack via .NET app .config tampering Installation High
Detects writes of a .NET application configuration file (appname.exe.config) containing an `appDomainManagerAssembly` / `appDomainManagerType` entry that redirects CLR initialization to a sideloaded assembly. This is the core Screening Serpens 2026 evolution that disables target app security and loads MiniUpdate/MiniJunk V2 RATs. Rationale: Targets the specific Unit 42-described evolution: AppDomainManager hijacking that manipulates .NET initialization via a legitimate .config file. The pattern of a same-directory triple (legitimate signed EXE + attacker EXE.config + attacker DLL) in user-writable paths is highly specific to this campaign and rarely seen in legitimate software, which always installs to Program Files via MSI/trusted installers. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/014/ • https://pentestlab.blog/2020/05/20/persistence-appdomainmanager/ • https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/iranian-cyber-actors-target-europe/
ATT&CKT1574.014 T1574.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName endswith ".exe.config"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Users\", @"\AppData\", @"\Temp\", @"\Downloads\", @"\ProgramData\")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msiexec.exe","TrustedInstaller.exe","wusa.exe","setup.exe","installer.exe","OfficeClickToRun.exe","GoogleUpdate.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files (x86)"
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName endswith ".dll"
    | where FolderPath has_any (@"\Users\", @"\AppData\", @"\Temp\", @"\Downloads\", @"\ProgramData\")
    | project DllTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, DllFolder=FolderPath, DllName=FileName, DllSHA256=SHA256, DllWriter=InitiatingProcessFileName
) on DeviceId
| where abs(datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, DllTime)) < 300 and tolower(FolderPath) == tolower(DllFolder)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, ConfigPath=FolderPath, ConfigName=FileName, DllName, DllSHA256, DllWriter, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let configWrites = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName endswith ".exe.config"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Users\", @"\AppData\", @"\Temp\", @"\Downloads\", @"\ProgramData\")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("msiexec.exe","TrustedInstaller.exe","wusa.exe","setup.exe","OfficeClickToRun.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ConfigPath=TargetFilePath, ConfigName=TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine;
let dllWrites = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName endswith ".dll"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Users\", @"\AppData\", @"\Temp\", @"\Downloads\", @"\ProgramData\")
| project DllTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DllPath=TargetFilePath, DllName=TargetFileName, DllSHA256=TargetFileSHA256;
configWrites
| join kind=inner dllWrites on DvcHostname
| where abs(datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, DllTime)) < 300
| extend ConfigDir = substring(ConfigPath, 0, strlen(ConfigPath) - strlen(ConfigName))
| extend DllDir = substring(DllPath, 0, strlen(DllPath) - strlen(DllName))
| where tolower(ConfigDir) == tolower(DllDir)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ConfigPath, ConfigName, DllName, DllSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:(*.exe.config OR *.EXE.config OR *.exe.CONFIG)) (@TargetFilename:(*\\Users\\* OR *\\AppData\\* OR *\\Temp\\* OR *\\Downloads\\* OR *\\ProgramData\\*)) -@Image:(*\\msiexec.exe OR *\\MsiExec.exe OR *\\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\\OfficeClickToRun.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\.exe\.config$/i
| TargetFileName=/\\(Users|AppData|Temp|Downloads|ProgramData)\\/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(msiexec|TrustedInstaller|OfficeClickToRun|GoogleUpdate|wusa|setup)\.exe$/i
| join({#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\.dll$/i | TargetFileName=/\\(Users|AppData|Temp|Downloads|ProgramData)\\/i}, field=aid, key=DllAid, include=[TargetFileName, SHA256HashData, _time])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())

[LLM] Screening Serpens C2 — DNS/network to UNC1549 infrastructure (Feb-Apr 2026) Command & Control High
Detects any DNS resolution or network connection to the four Unit 42-published Screening Serpens C2 domains used during the Feb-Apr 2026 espionage campaign against US, Israel, UAE and Middle Eastern targets. These domains are dedicated per-target/per-variant and seeing any single resolution is high-fidelity. Rationale: All four domains are explicitly named in the Unit 42 article as Screening Serpens C2 infrastructure for the Feb-Apr 2026 MiniUpdate/MiniJunk V2 campaign. The note `buisness-centeral-transportation.com` (deliberate typosquat of `business-central-transportation`) and `ramiltonsfinance.com` are highly unusual lures unlikely to appear in benign traffic. Cross-checked against MITRE G1019 (UNC1549) and Check Point's earlier Western Europe expansion report. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1019/ • https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/iranian-cyber-actors-target-europe/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004 T1583.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
let c2Domains = dynamic(["business-startup.org","buisness-centeral-transportation.com","premierhealthadvisory.com","ramiltonsfinance.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (c2Domains) or RemoteUrl endswith ".business-startup.org" or RemoteUrl endswith ".buisness-centeral-transportation.com" or RemoteUrl endswith ".premierhealthadvisory.com" or RemoteUrl endswith ".ramiltonsfinance.com"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
let c2Domains = dynamic(["business-startup.org","buisness-centeral-transportation.com","premierhealthadvisory.com","ramiltonsfinance.com"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where Name has_any (c2Domains)
| project TimeGenerated, Source="DnsEvents", Host=Computer, SrcIp=ClientIP, Query=Name, RemoteIp=tostring(IPAddresses)),
(ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where DnsQuery has_any (c2Domains)
| project TimeGenerated, Source="ImDnsActivity", Host=SrcHostname, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, Query=DnsQuery, RemoteIp=tostring(DnsResponseName)),
(CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where DestinationHostName has_any (c2Domains) or DestinationDnsDomain has_any (c2Domains) or RequestURL has_any (c2Domains)
| project TimeGenerated, Source="CommonSecurityLog", Host=SourceHostName, SrcIp=SourceIP, Query=coalesce(DestinationHostName, DestinationDnsDomain, RequestURL), RemoteIp=DestinationIP),
(ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where Url has_any (c2Domains) or HttpHostName has_any (c2Domains)
| project TimeGenerated, Source="ImWebSession", Host=SrcHostname, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, Query=coalesce(HttpHostName, Url), RemoteIp=DstIpAddr)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

(source:windows.sysmon OR source:windows.security OR source:zeek OR source:cisco-umbrella OR source:cloudflare) (@dns.question.name:(*business-startup.org OR *buisness-centeral-transportation.com OR *premierhealthadvisory.com OR *ramiltonsfinance.com) OR @network.destination.domain:(*business-startup.org OR *buisness-centeral-transportation.com OR *premierhealthadvisory.com OR *ramiltonsfinance.com) OR @http.url:(*business-startup.org* OR *buisness-centeral-transportation.com* OR *premierhealthadvisory.com* OR *ramiltonsfinance.com*) OR @QueryName:(*business-startup.org OR *buisness-centeral-transportation.com OR *premierhealthadvisory.com OR *ramiltonsfinance.com))

[LLM] Screening Serpens recruitment lure — Hiring Portal.zip + job requisition PDFs Delivery High
Detects delivery of the Screening Serpens spear-phishing lure: an archive named Hiring Portal.zip (or nested within an outer ZIP) accompanied by job-requisition PDFs following the pattern '*Software Engineer*Job ID JR######*.pdf'. Targets technical personnel in aerospace, defense and telecom sectors. Rationale: Pivots on the specific lure filename `Hiring Portal.zip` named by Unit 42 (and previously by Check Point research as a Screening Serpens artifact), plus the documented job-requisition PDF pattern (e.g., `Senior Software Engineer Job ID JR205894.pdf`). Restricting to user-download locations cuts the FP rate from generic HR keyword matches on email gateways. Cross-checked against: • https://research.checkpoint.com/2025/iranian-cyber-actors-target-europe/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1019/
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002 T1036.005
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Filesystem
let lureFileNames = dynamic(["Hiring Portal.zip","Hiring_Portal.zip","HiringPortal.zip"]);
let email = EmailAttachmentInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where FileName in~ (lureFileNames) or FileName matches regex @"(?i)^.*Software Engineer.*Job ID JR\d{6}.*\.pdf$" or FileName matches regex @"(?i)^.*Senior.*Engineer.*Job ID JR\d{6}.*\.pdf$"
| join kind=leftouter (EmailEvents | project NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation) on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, FileName, FileType, SHA256, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation;
let host = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where (FileName in~ (lureFileNames)) or (FileName matches regex @"(?i)^.*(Software|Senior|Principal).*Engineer.*Job ID JR\d{6}.*\.pdf$")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Desktop\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, FileOriginUrl;
union email, host
| order by Timestamp desc
let lureFileNames = dynamic(["Hiring Portal.zip","Hiring_Portal.zip","HiringPortal.zip"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where TargetFileName in~ (lureFileNames) or TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)^.*(Software|Senior|Principal).*Engineer.*Job ID JR\d{6}.*\.pdf$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\Desktop\", @"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Screening Serpens Hiring Portal Lure Archive
id: 4b8c2e15-d6f3-4e1a-9a7c-5e2f8b3d917a
description: Detects creation of the Hiring Portal.zip archive used as the Screening Serpens (UNC1549) MiniUpdate/MiniJunk V2 spear-phishing lure (Unit 42, May 2026).
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/tracking-iran-apt-screening-serpens/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/23
tags:
  - attack.t1566.001
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_archive:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\Hiring Portal.zip'
      - '\Hiring_Portal.zip'
      - '\HiringPortal.zip'
  selection_pdf:
    TargetFilename|re: '(?i).*(Software|Senior|Principal).*Engineer.*Job ID JR\d{6}.*\.pdf$'
  user_paths:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\Downloads\'
      - '\Desktop\'
      - '\Temp\'
  condition: (selection_archive or selection_pdf) and user_paths
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR email.proofpoint OR email.mimecast OR office365) (@TargetFilename:(*\\Hiring\ Portal.zip OR *\\Hiring_Portal.zip OR *\\HiringPortal.zip) OR @attachment.filename:("Hiring Portal.zip" OR Hiring_Portal.zip OR HiringPortal.zip) OR @email.subject:(*Hiring\ Portal* OR *Job\ Requisition* OR *JR205894*) OR @TargetFilename:(*Software\ Engineer*Job\ ID\ JR* OR *Senior*Engineer*Job\ ID\ JR*))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| (TargetFileName=/\\Hiring[\s_]?Portal\.zip$/i OR TargetFileName=/(Software|Senior|Principal).*Engineer.*Job ID JR\d{6}.*\.pdf$/i)
| TargetFileName=/\\(Downloads|Desktop|Temp)\\/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("business-startup.org", "buisness-centeral-transportation.com", "premierhealthadvisory.com", "ramiltonsfinance.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["business-startup.org", "buisness-centeral-transportation.com", "premierhealthadvisory.com", "ramiltonsfinance.com"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    - attack.t1555.003

logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:

            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'

            - '\opera.exe'

falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"

    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

let BadHashes = dynamic(["44f4f7aca7f1d9bfdaf7b3736934cbe19f851a707662f8f0b0c49b383e054250", "332ba2f0297dfb1599adecc3e9067893e7cf243aa23aedce4906a4c480574c17", "0db36a04d304ad96f9e6f97b531934594cd95a5cea9ff2c9af249201089dc864", "38bd137c672bd58d08c4f0502f993a6561e2c3411773d1ae57ee0151a0a9d11d", "d4a7e9f107fe40c1a5d0139c6c6e25bf6bf57f61feff090bee28f476bb3cc3c2", "bc3b44154518c5794ce639108e7b9c5fecb0c189607a26de1aaed518d890c7ad", "74882085db2088356ed7f72f01e0404a0a98cda88ef56fb15ce74c1f36b26d27", "9cf029daca89523d917dafed0568d11d00e45ec96b5b90b4a1f7fd4018c7da84", "b19e06da580cf91691eda066ac9ee4b09c6e5dc26c367af12660fe1f9306eec4", "8808c794c24367438f183e4be941876f1d3ecd0c8d2eb43b10d2380841d2283b", "43dc62cef52ebdd69e79f10015b3e13890f26c058325c0ff139c70f8d8eadcfa", "9e4a658e6d831c9e9bdfe11884a75b7c64812ed0a80e8495ddf6b316505acac1"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Megalodon CI/CD C2 beacon to 216.126.225.129:8443 Command & Control High
Detects any outbound connection to the Megalodon campaign C2 endpoint (216.126.225.129:8443) used to exfiltrate CI secrets, AWS/GCP/Azure credentials, SSH keys, OIDC tokens, and source-code secrets harvested by base64-encoded bash payloads injected into GitHub Actions workflows. Catches both self-hosted runners executing the poisoned workflow and any developer workstation that cloned and ran a compromised pipeline. Rationale: C2 IP 216.126.225.129:8443 is named verbatim in SafeDep's primary write-up and reproduced in cross-coverage from cybersecuritynews.com, cybernews.com, hackread.com — a stable, single-purpose exfil endpoint. Any successful TCP connect to that pair from org telemetry is high-confidence compromise; no legitimate service known at that destination. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/megalodon-mass-github-repo-backdooring-ci-workflows/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/megalodon-malware-github-repos/ • https://hackread.com/github-repositories-megalodon-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041 T1567
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP == "216.126.225.129"
| where RemotePort == 8443
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, LocalIP
| order by Timestamp desc
let MegalodonC2 = "216.126.225.129";
union isfuzzy=true
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where DestinationIP == MegalodonC2 and DestinationPort == 8443
        | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, DeviceAction, RequestURL, SourceHostName),
    (ImNetworkSession
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where DstIpAddr == MegalodonC2 and DstPortNumber == 8443
        | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, DvcHostname)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Polymarket npm wallet drainer egress to polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev Actions on Objectives High
Detects DNS resolution or HTTP egress to polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev — the Cloudflare Worker endpoint used by the nine malicious polymarketdev npm packages (polymarket-trading-cli, polymarket-bot, polymarket-claude-code, etc.) to receive Ethereum/Polygon private keys pasted into the fake postinstall onboarding prompt. Path /v1/wallets/keys is the receive endpoint. Rationale: Domain `polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev` and the receive path `/v1/wallets/keys` are both stated verbatim in SafeDep's report and reproduced by StepSecurity's separate investigation of the polymarketdev/dev-protocol GitHub org takeover. Cloudflare Workers subdomains under a single throwaway account are single-purpose — any DNS hit is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/malicious-polymarket-npm-crypto-wallet-drainer/ • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/malicious-polymarket-bot-hides-in-hijacked-dev-protocol-github-org-and-steals-wallet-keys
ATT&CKT1567 T1041 T1552.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
let badHost = "polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev";
union isfuzzy=true
  (DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where RemoteUrl has badHost
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort),
  (DeviceEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ActionType in ("DnsQueryResponse", "ConnectionSuccess", "ConnectionFailed")
    | where RemoteUrl has badHost or AdditionalFields has badHost
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, AdditionalFields)
| order by Timestamp desc
let badHost = "polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev";
union isfuzzy=true
    (DnsEvents | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where Name endswith badHost or Name has badHost | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCode),
    (ImDnsActivity | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DnsQuery endswith badHost or DnsQuery has badHost | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DnsQuery, DnsResponseCodeName),
    (ImWebSession | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where HttpHostName endswith badHost or Url has badHost | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Url, HttpMethod, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent),
    (CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where RequestURL has badHost or DestinationDnsDomain has badHost | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, RequestURL, DestinationDnsDomain, DeviceProduct)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Polymarket npm persistence: ~/.polybot/ directory written by node/npm Installation High
Detects creation of files under the ~/.polybot/ persistence directory by node or npm processes. The malicious polymarketdev packages create this directory on first install to drop a device-fingerprint file that allows the operator to track victims across sessions, even before the user pastes a private key. Catches infections that fired but where the C2 egress was blocked or not yet observed. Rationale: SafeDep's polymarket write-up names `~/.polybot/` as the persistence + device-fingerprint directory created by the postinstall hook before the user even sees the wallet prompt; the directory name does not collide with any known legitimate Node tool. Pairing the path with node/npm/npx parent process keeps the rule from firing on coincidental directory names. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/malicious-polymarket-npm-crypto-wallet-drainer/
ATT&CKT1547 T1546.016 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed", "FileModified")
| where FolderPath has "/.polybot/" or FolderPath has @"\.polybot\"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node", "node.exe", "npm", "npm.exe", "npx", "npx.exe", "yarn", "yarn.exe", "pnpm", "pnpm.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed", "FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath has "/.polybot/" or TargetFilePath has @"\.polybot\"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node", "node.exe", "npm", "npm.exe", "npx", "npx.exe", "yarn", "yarn.exe", "pnpm", "pnpm.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Megalodon CI runner: shell scraping /proc/*/environ for in-memory secrets Installation Medium
Detects shell or coreutils processes reading /proc/*/environ — the credential-harvesting fingerprint used by the Megalodon GitHub Actions payload to scrape every running process's environment variables (GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_*, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, Vault tokens, etc.) on a self-hosted runner. The article explicitly states the payload reads `/proc/*/environ, and PID 1 environment` — a behaviour vanishingly rare in legitimate CI workflows. Rationale: The article explicitly lists "/proc/*/environ, and PID 1 environment" as one of the first data classes the Megalodon harvester collects — that's a unique behavioural string we can pivot on. Combining `/proc/*/environ` access with shell/coreutils parents distinguishes the attack from a developer running `cat /proc/$$/environ` once for debugging. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/megalodon-mass-github-repo-backdooring-ci-workflows/ • https://cybernews.com/security/megalodon-github-5000-repos-backdooring-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1083 T1057 T1212
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/proc/" and ProcessCommandLine has "/environ"
| where FileName in~ ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh", "cat", "grep", "awk", "find", "xargs", "tr", "strings", "head", "tail")
    or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where (ActingProcessCommandLine has "/proc/" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "/environ")
    or (TargetProcessCommandLine has "/proc/" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "/environ")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh", "cat", "grep", "awk", "find", "xargs", "tr", "strings")
    or TargetProcessName has_any ("cat", "grep", "awk", "find", "xargs", "tr", "strings")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Megalodon CI Runner /proc/*/environ Mass Secret Scrape
id: cd4e5f6a-7b8c-9d0e-1f2a-3b4c5d6e7f8a
description: Detects shell or coreutils processes reading /proc/*/environ on Linux — the credential-harvesting pattern named in the Megalodon CI/CD payload that scrapes every running process's environment block for CI secrets, GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS/GCP/Azure credentials, and OIDC tokens injected by GitHub Actions. Legitimate use of /proc/*/environ from a shell is rare outside debugging or forensic tools.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/megalodon-github-attack-targets-5561.html
  - https://safedep.io/megalodon-mass-github-repo-backdooring-ci-workflows/
author: Detection Team
date: 2026/05/23
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.discovery
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.t1083
  - attack.t1057
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
      - '/cat'
      - '/grep'
      - '/awk'
      - '/find'
      - '/xargs'
      - '/tr'
      - '/strings'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/proc/'
      - '/environ'
  condition: selection_image and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
  - Forensic / DFIR triage tooling intentionally enumerating process environments
  - Performance diagnostics scripts inspecting a single PID's environ (lower /proc cardinality)
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.command_line:*/proc/*/environ* OR @process.executable.path:(/usr/bin/cat OR /bin/cat OR /usr/bin/grep OR /usr/bin/awk OR /usr/bin/find OR /usr/bin/xargs OR /usr/bin/strings)) AND @process.command_line:*environ*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 CommandLine=/\/proc\/[^\s\/]+\/environ/
| ImageFileName=/(bash|sh|dash|zsh|cat|grep|awk|find|xargs|tr|strings|head|tail)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine, UserName], function=count())
| count > 0
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process="*/proc/*" Processes.process="*/environ*" (Processes.process_name=bash OR Processes.process_name=sh OR Processes.process_name=dash OR Processes.process_name=zsh OR Processes.process_name=cat OR Processes.process_name=grep OR Processes.process_name=awk OR Processes.process_name=find OR Processes.process_name=xargs OR Processes.process_name=tr OR Processes.process_name=strings) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process="*/proc/*" Processes.process="*/environ*" (Processes.process_name=bash OR Processes.process_name=sh OR Processes.process_name=dash OR Processes.process_name=zsh OR Processes.process_name=cat OR Processes.process_name=grep OR Processes.process_name=awk OR Processes.process_name=find OR Processes.process_name=xargs OR Processes.process_name=tr OR Processes.process_name=strings) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("216.126.225.129") or RemoteUrl has_any ("polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["216.126.225.129"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev"]);
ImNetworkSession

| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)

| order by TimeGenerated desc

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")

| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"

      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Ethereum\keystore\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Bitcoin\wallet.dat"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Exodus\exodus.wallet*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Electrum\wallets\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\MetaMask\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Phantom\*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName

// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or SHA1 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or MD5 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or SHA1 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or MD5 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Making Vulnerable Drivers Exploitable Without Hardware - The BYOVD Perspective

The Hacker News
2026-05-22 8 use cases 4 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

1 Introduction This article provides a technical analysis of how many Windows kernel mode drivers can be interacted with from user mode without the hardware they were developed for. This work was motivated by driver-oriented vulnerability research and the need to evaluate the exploitability of individual findings, which frequently affect code whose reachability is hardware-gated. Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Driver .sys dropped to System32\drivers by user-context process
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Making Vulnerable Drivers Exploitable Without Hardware - The BYOVD Perspective
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] BYOVD kernel-driver service deployment via sc.exe create + start correlation · [LLM] Kernel-type service registry creation with .sys ImagePath by user-context process
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] BYOVD kernel-driver service deployment via sc.exe create + start correlation Installation High
Detects the exact two-step BYOVD deployment sequence the article calls out: `sc.exe create <name> type= kernel start= demand binPath= System32\drivers\<x>.sys` followed by `sc.exe start <name>` on the same host. Sharpens the canonical SigmaHQ kernel-driver rule by requiring the start-follow-up + a .sys binPath ending, eliminating sysadmin driver-install noise. Rationale: Anchored on the article's literal deployment command (`sc.exe create ... type= kernel start= demand binPath= System32\drivers\<x>.sys` + `sc.exe start <name>`). The temporal correlation between create+start within 10min on the same service name is what differentiates BYOVD operator behaviour from a sysadmin reading docs. Cross-checked SigmaHQ `proc_creation_win_sc_new_kernel_driver.yml` and confirmed the canonical rule does NOT correlate the start follow-up — that's the value-add here. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/proc_creation_win_sc_new_kernel_driver.yml • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068/ • https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/scattered-spider-attempts-to-avoid-detection-with-bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver-tactic/ • https://www.picussecurity.com/resource/blog/what-are-bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver-byovd-attacks
ATT&CKT1068 T1562.001 T1543.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowSeconds = 600;
let Creates = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where FileName =~ "sc.exe"
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "create"
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "type=" and ProcessCommandLine has "kernel"
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "binPath="
    | where ProcessCommandLine has ".sys"
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | extend SvcName = extract(@"(?i)create\s+(\S+)\s", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
    | project CreateTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, CreateCmd = ProcessCommandLine, ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName, SvcName;
let Starts = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where FileName =~ "sc.exe"
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "start"
    | extend StartedSvc = extract(@"(?i)\bstart\s+(\S+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
    | project StartTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, StartedSvc, StartCmd = ProcessCommandLine;
Creates
| join kind=inner Starts on DeviceId
| where StartTime between (CreateTime .. CreateTime + WindowSeconds * 1s)
| where tolower(SvcName) == tolower(StartedSvc)
| project CreateTime, StartTime, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', StartTime, CreateTime), DeviceName, AccountName, SvcName, CreateCmd, StartCmd, ParentImage
| order by CreateTime desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowSeconds = 600;
let Creates = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName endswith "\\sc.exe"
    | where CommandLine has "create"
    | where CommandLine has "type=" and CommandLine has "kernel"
    | where CommandLine has "binPath=" and CommandLine has ".sys"
    | where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
    | extend SvcName = extract(@"(?i)create\s+(\S+)\s", 1, CommandLine)
    | project CreateTime = TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, CreateCmd = CommandLine, ParentName = ParentProcessName, SvcName;
let Starts = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName endswith "\\sc.exe"
    | where CommandLine has "start"
    | extend StartedSvc = extract(@"(?i)\bstart\s+(\S+)", 1, CommandLine)
    | project StartTime = TimeGenerated, Computer, StartedSvc, StartCmd = CommandLine;
Creates
| join kind=inner Starts on Computer
| where StartTime between (CreateTime .. CreateTime + WindowSeconds * 1s)
| where tolower(SvcName) == tolower(StartedSvc)
| project CreateTime, StartTime, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', StartTime, CreateTime), Computer, SubjectUserName, SvcName, CreateCmd, StartCmd, ParentName
| order by CreateTime desc
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) (@EventID:1 OR @EventID:4688) @Image:(*\\sc.exe OR *\\SC.exe OR *\\SC.EXE) @CommandLine:(*create* *type=* *kernel* *binPath=* *.sys*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\sc\.exe$/i CommandLine=/create/i CommandLine=/type=\s*kernel/i CommandLine=/binPath=/i CommandLine=/\.sys/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine], function=count())
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\sc\.exe$/i CommandLine=/\bstart\b/i}, field=aid, include=[CommandLine, _time])

[LLM] Kernel-type service registry creation with .sys ImagePath by user-context process Installation Medium
Detects the registry artefact of any BYOVD service install — a new value under `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\<name>\` where `Type=0x1` (kernel driver) and `ImagePath` references a .sys outside the protected DriverStore. Catches BYOVD frameworks that bypass sc.exe and write the registry directly (CreateServiceW / advapi32). Rationale: Article §3.1 names the registry-and-service install pattern (`sc.exe create ... type= kernel ... binPath= System32\drivers\X.sys`) as the BYOVD prerequisite, and the registry artefact persists even when attackers skip sc.exe entirely (calling CreateServiceW directly). Sysmon EID 13 captures both `Type` and `ImagePath` writes; pairing them on the same service name + filtering DriverStore + TrustedInstaller eliminates Windows Update / OEM driver noise. Cross-checked against CrowdStrike's Scattered Spider BYOVD writeup which lists the same registry hive as the canonical pivot. Cross-checked against: • https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/scattered-spider-attempts-to-avoid-detection-with-bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver-tactic/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543/003/ • https://www.splunk.com/en_us/blog/security/these-are-the-drivers-you-are-looking-for-detect-and-prevent-malicious-drivers.html
ATT&CKT1543.003 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
let TypeWrites = DeviceRegistryEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
    | where RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\SYSTEM\\(CurrentControlSet|ControlSet00\d)\\Services\\[^\\]+$"
    | where RegistryValueName =~ "Type"
    | where RegistryValueData in ("1","0x1","0x00000001")
    | extend SvcName = tostring(split(RegistryKey, "\\")[-1])
    | project TypeTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, SvcName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
let ImageWrites = DeviceRegistryEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
    | where RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\SYSTEM\\(CurrentControlSet|ControlSet00\d)\\Services\\[^\\]+$"
    | where RegistryValueName =~ "ImagePath"
    | where RegistryValueData has ".sys"
    | where RegistryValueData !contains "\\DriverStore\\"
    | extend SvcName = tostring(split(RegistryKey, "\\")[-1])
    | project ImageTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, SvcName, ImagePath = RegistryValueData;
TypeWrites
| join kind=inner ImageWrites on DeviceId, SvcName
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","msiexec.exe","services.exe","setup.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project TypeTime, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, SvcName, ImagePath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by TypeTime desc
Event
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Source == "Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon" and EventID == 13
| extend ed = parse_xml(EventData)
| extend TargetObject = tostring(ed.DataItem.EventData.Data[3].["#text"])
| extend Details = tostring(ed.DataItem.EventData.Data[4].["#text"])
| extend ImageProc = tostring(ed.DataItem.EventData.Data[5].["#text"])
| where TargetObject matches regex @"(?i)\\SYSTEM\\(CurrentControlSet|ControlSet00\d)\\Services\\[^\\]+\\(Type|ImagePath)$"
| extend SvcName = extract(@"(?i)\\Services\\([^\\]+)\\", 1, TargetObject)
| extend Field = extract(@"(?i)\\([^\\]+)$", 1, TargetObject)
| summarize TypeVal = anyif(Details, Field =~ "Type"), ImageVal = anyif(Details, Field =~ "ImagePath"), Proc = any(ImageProc), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated) by Computer, SvcName
| where TypeVal in ("1","0x1","DWORD (0x00000001)") and ImageVal has ".sys"
| where ImageVal !contains "\\DriverStore\\"
| where Proc !endswith "\\TrustedInstaller.exe" and Proc !endswith "\\msiexec.exe" and Proc !endswith "\\services.exe"
| project FirstSeen, Computer, SvcName, ImageVal, Proc
| order by FirstSeen desc
title: New Kernel-Type Service Registered with Non-DriverStore .sys ImagePath
id: 8f3c7d22-ba1e-4e7e-9a45-3f7b1d4f9d22
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of a Windows service registry key with Type=0x1 (kernel driver) whose ImagePath references a .sys file outside the protected DriverStore. Used by BYOVD frameworks that drop a vulnerable driver and register it as a kernel service for IRP reachability.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/making-vulnerable-drivers-exploitable.html
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543/003/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/23
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1543.003
  - attack.t1562.001
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.privilege_escalation
logsource:
  category: registry_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_type:
    TargetObject|re: '(?i)\\SYSTEM\\(CurrentControlSet|ControlSet00\d)\\Services\\[^\\]+\\Type$'
    Details:
      - 'DWORD (0x00000001)'
      - '0x00000001'
      - '0x1'
      - '1'
  filter_trusted:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\TrustedInstaller.exe'
      - '\msiexec.exe'
      - '\services.exe'
  condition: selection_type and not filter_trusted
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate signed third-party driver installation (printer, GPU, VPN, AV)
  - Endpoint management tooling (SCCM/Intune) deploying drivers via custom scripts
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:13 @TargetObject:(*\\Services\\*\\Type OR *\\Services\\*\\ImagePath OR *\\services\\*\\type OR *\\services\\*\\imagepath) -@Image:(*\\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\\trustedinstaller.exe OR *\\msiexec.exe OR *\\MSIEXEC.exe OR *\\services.exe)
#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate RegObjectName=/\\Services\\[^\\]+$/i (RegValueName=/^Type$/i OR RegValueName=/^ImagePath$/i)
| case {
    RegValueName=/^Type$/i RegStringValue=/^(1|0x0*1)$/ | KernelType:="true";
    RegValueName=/^ImagePath$/i RegStringValue=/\.sys/i NOT RegStringValue=/\\DriverStore\\/i | HasDriverPath:="true";
  }
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RegObjectName], function={ collect([RegValueName, RegStringValue, ContextImageFileName, KernelType, HasDriverPath]) })
| KernelType="true" HasDriverPath="true"
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(TrustedInstaller|msiexec|services)\.exe$/i
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Registry.registry_value_data) as value_data values(Registry.process_path) as proc_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path="*\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\*\\Type" Registry.registry_value_data="0x00000001" by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.registry_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | rex field=registry_path "Services\\\\(?<svc_name>[^\\\\]+)\\\\Type" | join type=inner svc_name [| tstats `summariesonly` values(Registry.registry_value_data) as image_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path="*\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\*\\ImagePath" by Registry.registry_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | rex field=registry_path "Services\\\\(?<svc_name>[^\\\\]+)\\\\ImagePath"] | where like(image_path,"%.sys%") AND NOT like(image_path,"%\\DriverStore\\%") AND NOT like(proc_path,"%\\TrustedInstaller.exe") AND NOT like(proc_path,"%\\msiexec.exe") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | table firstTime, dest, user, svc_name, image_path, proc_path
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Registry.registry_value_data) as value_data values(Registry.process_path) as proc_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path="*\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\*\\Type" Registry.registry_value_data="0x00000001" by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.registry_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | rex field=registry_path "Services\\\\(?<svc_name>[^\\\\]+)\\\\Type" | join type=inner svc_name [| tstats summariesonly=false values(Registry.registry_value_data) as image_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path="*\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\*\\ImagePath" by Registry.registry_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | rex field=registry_path "Services\\\\(?<svc_name>[^\\\\]+)\\\\ImagePath"] | where like(image_path,"%.sys%") AND NOT like(image_path,"%\\DriverStore\\%") AND NOT like(proc_path,"%\\TrustedInstaller.exe") AND NOT like(proc_path,"%\\msiexec.exe") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | table firstTime, dest, user, svc_name, image_path, proc_path
[LLM] Driver .sys dropped to System32\drivers by user-context process Delivery Medium
Detects the BYOVD file-staging step: a .sys file written into `C:\Windows\System32\drivers\` (the canonical binPath target in the article's deployment command) by a process that is not TrustedInstaller, msiexec, Windows Update or the DriverStore. Pre-stages the alert before the sc.exe service-create fires, giving SOC a chance to catch the drop pre-load. Rationale: Article §3.1 deployment command names `System32\drivers\<x>.sys` as the binPath target. Any .sys landing there from a non-installer process is the pre-load BYOVD staging step. SHA256 from this hit feeds straight into a loldrivers.io / Microsoft Vulnerable Driver Blocklist lookup. Filtering DriverStore/WinSxS/TrustedInstaller is what makes this rule production-viable rather than dashboard noise — confirmed against Splunk's published guidance on driver-write monitoring. Cross-checked against: • https://www.splunk.com/en_us/blog/security/these-are-the-drivers-you-are-looking-for-detect-and-prevent-malicious-drivers.html • https://reversingops.com/posts/detecting-driver-loading-techniques/ • https://loldrivers.io/
ATT&CKT1068 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)\\Windows\\System32\\drivers\\?$"
| where FileName endswith ".sys"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","msiexec.exe","drvinst.exe","wuauclt.exe","MoUsoCoreWorker.exe","setup.exe","DismHost.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\Windows\\System32\\DriverStore\\"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, SHA256, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)\\Windows\\System32\\drivers\\[^\\]+\.sys$"
| where ActingProcessName !endswith "\\TrustedInstaller.exe"
  and ActingProcessName !endswith "\\msiexec.exe"
  and ActingProcessName !endswith "\\drvinst.exe"
  and ActingProcessName !endswith "\\wuauclt.exe"
  and ActingProcessName !endswith "\\DismHost.exe"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine !contains "\\DriverStore\\"
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$" and ActorUsername !in~ ("SYSTEM","LOCAL SERVICE","NETWORK SERVICE")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Driver File Dropped to System32 Drivers Directory by User Context
id: 1b2e9c44-7c84-4ad1-a3e8-04a0fbc63bea
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of a .sys file in C:\Windows\System32\drivers by a process that is not TrustedInstaller, msiexec, drvinst, or the Windows Update stack. Article-anchored on the BYOVD deployment target path documented by Atos research.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/making-vulnerable-drivers-exploitable.html
  - https://loldrivers.io/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/23
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.privilege_escalation
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|re: '(?i)\\Windows\\System32\\drivers\\[^\\]+\.sys$'
  filter_installers:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\TrustedInstaller.exe'
      - '\msiexec.exe'
      - '\drvinst.exe'
      - '\wuauclt.exe'
      - '\DismHost.exe'
      - '\MoUsoCoreWorker.exe'

    Image|contains: '\Windows\WinSxS\'
  condition: selection and not 1 of filter_*
falsepositives:
  - Vendor MSI installers that bypass DrvInst
  - In-place Windows feature upgrade staging
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\\System32\\drivers\\*.sys OR *\\system32\\drivers\\*.sys OR *\\SYSTEM32\\DRIVERS\\*.sys) -@Image:(*\\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\\trustedinstaller.exe OR *\\msiexec.exe OR *\\drvinst.exe OR *\\DrvInst.exe OR *\\wuauclt.exe OR *\\DismHost.exe OR *\\MoUsoCoreWorker.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\\Windows\\System32\\drivers\\[^\\]+\.sys$/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(TrustedInstaller|msiexec|drvinst|wuauclt|DismHost|MoUsoCoreWorker)\.exe$/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\System32\\DriverStore\\/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\Windows\\WinSxS\\/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_path) as proc_path values(Filesystem.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path="*\\System32\\drivers\\*" Filesystem.file_name="*.sys" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | search NOT proc_path IN ("*\\TrustedInstaller.exe","*\\msiexec.exe","*\\drvinst.exe","*\\wuauclt.exe","*\\System32\\svchost.exe") | search NOT user IN ("*$","SYSTEM","LOCAL SERVICE","NETWORK SERVICE") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | table firstTime, dest, user, file_name, file_hash, proc_path
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.

DeviceProcessEvents
